children: Shares of Moderna
have rallied 202% since Aug. 18, fueled by positive news about the biotech company's experimental cancer vaccine, intismeran, which is being co-developed with Merck
Last week, analysts at Citigroup cut their rating of the stock to Sell, asserting that sales expectations for the treatment were "unrealistic."
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
and
if they thought Moderna
was now a Sell, given its massive recent run-up.
: Yes, Moderna's

valuation undeservedly tripled following Phase 3 melanoma results for its personalized mRNA cancer vaccine. While the science is promising, approval for high-risk melanoma would likely generate no more than $5B in peak annual sales, yet its valuation has risen over $50B since the news drop.
I'd also point out that we are not yet aware of any data details, like hazard ratio (HR), until Moderna
presents them later this month. If the HR is less impressive than what we saw in the Phase 2b trial (0.51), I suspect the market may be disappointed.
I also believe the market is getting ahead of itself by assuming Moderna's

vaccine will be effective across multiple cancer types. Melanoma is known as the "lowest-hanging fruit" in immuno-oncology because it is highly immunogenic and exceptionally responsive to immunotherapy relative to other solid tumors. Pricing in platform-wide validation based on a single immunogenic outlier could be a big mistake. So, I expect MRNA to "cool off" in October.
The Alpha Analyst: Moderna
is absolutely a Sell and has been so since it was testing the $150 mark recently.
The intismeran melanoma Phase 3 read with Merck

is a real step change, no doubt. But suppose I underwrite ~$5.7B of 2029 revenue, meaning melanoma plus a growing COVID/flu base, apply a generous 10x sales multiple, and discount back at 12%. That gets me to roughly $110 a share. Even that figure credits kidney, lung, and bladder cancers, of which none of the trials has read out, and each is a separate trial.

Holding that Sell position is the hard part, fighting against narrative and momentum. With money rotating from AI infrastructure into broader innovation bets, the stock can stay stretched longer than valuations suggest. Still, I see high odds of an eventual cooling, best expressed through limited-risk puts rather than an outright short.

The kidney cancer (RCC) readout is the next binary event that could either further extend the rally or break it. My tilt is that the kidney test will be tougher than melanoma (fewer mutations to target through this approach), so the stock could normalize around that readout, if not earlier.
